note: Visible changes to the ride, newest first. One entry per shipped fix the player can see; models themselves are listed by the feed. Fields: date (YYYY-MM-DD, the day it reached main), title, text, where [lng, lat] optional.

notes.title: Schools, cinemas and places of worship look more like themselves
notes.text: School buildings now take their brick colour from street photos or from the era they were built in, instead of one beige for all. Pre-war schools get their tiled hipped roofs, and 143 cinemas, churches, mosques, synagogues and temples that showed only a plain block now have coping and a plinth.

notes.title: Bridge cards say what the bridge register records again
notes.text: Named bridges such as the Blauwbrug once more show where the name comes from, the trivia, and the line from the city's bridge register (number, construction and year). The trivia had been replacing the whole card.

notes.title: Pavements, islands and verges fill the gaps beside roads
notes.text: Traffic islands, berms, verges and paved squares from the city's surface survey now fill what used to show as bare land next to the road. At the regression spots bare land beside carriageways fell by three quarters, and Mosplein no longer shows stray red.

notes.title: Behind-bike camera tilts again; W no longer opens Wikipedia
notes.text: The chase camera had been set flatter than the top-down views, so 'behind bike' looked top-down and half the tilt slider did nothing. It now starts low behind the bike and the whole slider tilts. Steering with W no longer opens monument articles (that moved to E), and D no longer toggles street labels (now T).

notes.title: The 3D city comes back after the graphics card resets
notes.text: When a phone dropped and regained its graphics context, the ground, trees, buildings and bike stayed blank until a reload. They now rebuild within a second; building facades repaint over the following seconds.

notes.title: Roads: no more doubled lanes or guessed paint
notes.text: OSM road bands no longer draw over the measured road surfaces, so the stray red cycle pieces and double lanes are gone (De Clercqstraat, Rozengracht, Spiegelgracht). Cycle-lane red, centre dashes and zebras are now drawn only where the 8 cm aerial photo shows them; nearby zebras merge into one. Phones also keep only the ground they can see, which more than halves ground memory.

notes.title: Nassaukade: the orange wedge above the cornice is gone
notes.text: A narrow, deep row house with no mapped roof type could be dealt a half-hip roof, whose bare street end showed as an orange wedge between taller crowned neighbours. Such plots now get the row's gable crown instead. Phones also keep fewer ground cells resident behind the rider.

notes.title: Phones use far less memory
notes.text: The map no longer keeps a second copy of every streamed building on phones, and the painted facade canvases are freed once their textures are built. A frame error no longer freezes the ride.

notes.title: Three roofs fixed from your feedback
notes.text: The Academie voor Theater en Dans roof had an open edge; the Booking.com block on Utrechtsestraat had a crumpled rooftop and is now flat above its fronts; the Anne Frank statue plate no longer flickers against its plinth.

notes.title: Gables face the street
notes.text: Canal and 19th-century houses whose only street front was the long side had their ridge running along the street, so the gable faced the neighbour. Ridges now turn across the front; wide fronts split into several gables.

notes.title: The ferry at Centraal works again
notes.text: Boarding at the Centraal pier could leave you stuck on a berth. The pier's berth shapes, the chain of stops and the access check were all fixed.
